scope: Package-independent native/MCP browser admission with deferred compatible visual model
sourceBinding: Final source hashes bind mcp-browser-without-package-final-01. Earlier intermediate revisions were not individually hashed. Exact commands, xcresult summaries, test identifiers, full task reports and failures remain retained.
policy: macOS MCP/native tools first; no computer-use model package required for sufficient browser steps.
One build/test at a time, Xcode jobs 1, no source edits during active builds/tests.
No llama inference, model downloads, purchases, messages, login, push, release or installed-host replacement.

browserAdmission.tested: Typed no-argument host route, explicit availability, unique tool name and single-capture/recovery boundaries.
browserAdmission.accepted: Scoped host routing; arbitrary mixed-domain tasks remain unqualified.

browserWithoutModelPackage.tested: Default manager composition, actual Apple planner and real installed MCP helper, production browser loader with missing native/visual receipts and a rejecting model launcher. Controlled full task completes in 10.720366 seconds; zero downloads/launch attempts/workers, one visit per page.
browserWithoutModelPackage.accepted: Controlled informational task through HostComputerUseManager, not full HostSession/provider/phone acceptance.

lateVisualDependency.tested: Absent, broken and available fixture packages all permit the first MCP proposal. After a scoped tool decline, absent/broken states reject before launch; valid fixture attempts one deliberately rejected launch. Same window/session/clarification retained.
lateVisualDependency.accepted: Package resolution and activation boundary; no real model inference in this checkpoint.

generalProductionComputerUse.tested: 16 final focused methods pass, zero skips; broader acceptance remains incomplete.

findings: Original host task fails before any navigation with visual-setup-required, despite available MCP helper and adequate native page records.
First implementation separates a browser route but still relies on a magic response token; four routing/continuation methods pass while the real task fails.

Transparent actual-planner diagnostics show a 1391-byte prompt with eight tools. The model says a browser operation is required but ignores the response token. This observed failure is format compliance, not a demonstrated context limit.

Final Foundation Models callback records a typed browser route, not an invented MCP server call. It has no URL, replacement goal, executor, model or application effects. Browser availability is explicit per planning request.
Browser and MCP proposals share the existing single-write capture. Only exact multiple-proposal recovery may preserve its first proposal; other generation errors are not masked.
Browser preparation is retained before execution. Changed goals, cancellation or factory failures cannot execute another route. Clarifications/approval continuation use the retained executor.

The production loader resolves Fara only when its visual proposal/page-reading callback is reached; absent or incompatible receipts do not prevent earlier MCP work. Model selection and resource caps are unchanged.
The final bundle records two main-thread responsiveness runtime warnings. Compiler diagnostics and wrapper lines are retained in full logs.
No production flicker, whole-Mac 12 GB/heat, real-provider login or physical-phone claim follows from the controlled tests.
